 Appearance:
 MR M.NISAR VAIDHYA(3386) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR MOHDDANISH M BAREJIA(10612) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR HK PATEL, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================

sentences.text: Learned APP waives service of notice of Rule for and on behalf of the respondent No.1 - State of Gujarat.

[1.0] By way of the present application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short "BNSS"), the applicant has prayed for anticipatory bail in the event of arrest in connection with the FIR being C.R. No. 11191011240325 of 2024 registered with DCB Police Station, Ahmedabad, for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 418 and 114 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 66(d) of IT Act.
[2.0] Learned advocate for the applicant submits that the applicant has nothing to do with the offence.
Though vide order dated 23.01.2025, it has been clearly mentioned that no notice under Section 35 of BNSS has been issued to the applicant, however,
Even prior to registration of FIR, the applicant has joined the investigation.
The applicant has no past antecedent.
However, the offence is punishable maximum upto 7 years imprisonment.
Therefore, custodial interrogation at this stage is not necessary.

Besides, the applicant is available during the course of investigation and will not flee Ajmeri Aiyubbhai Jusabbhai vs State Of Gujarat on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15957242/
1 from justice.

sentences.text: In view of the above, the applicant may be granted anticipatory NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/810/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/04/2025 undefined bail.
[3.0] Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent - State has opposed grant of anticipatory bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.
Offence prima facie reveals against the applicant.
Therefore, custodial interrogation is required.
Hence, application does not deserve any consideration.

[4.0] Having heard the learned advocate for the parties and perusing the investigation papers, it is equally incumbent upon the Court to exercise its discretion judiciously, cautiously and strictly in compliance with the basic principles laid down in a plethora of decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court on the point.

It is well settled that, among other circumstances, the factors to be borne in mind while considering an application for bail are (i) the nature and gravity of the accusation; (ii) the antecedents of the applicant including the fact as to whether he has previously undergone imprisonment on conviction by a Court in respect of any cognizable offence; (iii) the possibility of the applicant to flee from justice; and (iv) where the accusation has been made with the object of injuring or humiliating the applicant by having him so arrested.
Though at the stage of granting bail an elaborate examination of evidence and detailed reasons touching the merit of the case, which may prejudice the accused, should be avoided.
I have considered the following aspects.
(1) Even prior to registration of FIR, the applicant has joined investigation.
(2) Applicant has no past antecedent.
(3) Nothing is required to be recovered from the applicant.
(4) Offence is triable by JMFC Court.
(5) None of the offence alleged is punishable with life sent  penalty.
